category: machine translation API, one-time free character credit

free_tier.stated: a one-time credit of 1 million characters for text and document translation on the Developer plan: a total translation limit of 1,000,000 characters that does not reset; further use needs the paid Growth plan
free_tier.notes: the true unit is source characters (Unicode code points sent for translation); the schema vocabulary has no character unit, so mixed is the nearest term. The Developer plan does not include speech to text and does not include access to the web translator. The earlier DeepL API Free plan (500,000 characters per month) is a separate record

per_object_cap.stated: 128 KiB total request size and 16 KiB header size for every API plan; the document limit column for free plans is 10 MB and 500,000 characters for a Word file (whether the Developer plan uses that column is unverified)

retention.stated: not applicable: a translation endpoint stores nothing for the caller

tooling: HTTP REST API with the header 'Authorization: DeepL-Auth-Key <key>' and DeepL's own client libraries; JSON or form-encoded bodies. Free API keys are identified by the suffix ':fx' and use the host api-free.deepl.com; whether a Developer key carries that suffix and host is unverified: behind a sign-up
chaining: a lifetime credit of 1,000,000 characters, then the Growth plan at a card-only checkout; the credit does not recur, so it does not replace a recurring free translation route

limits.value: 1,000,000 characters in total, one time, does not reset
128 KiB total request size; 16 KiB header size
unverified: no request-rate figure is published; the API answers HTTP 429 for too many requests in a short period and HTTP 456 when a usage limit is reached

identity_cost.detail: the sign-up form is step 1 of 3 ('Sign up', 'Plan details', 'Get API key') and asks for an email, a password and a confirmation of being over 14; whether step 2 'Plan details' asks for a card or an address is unverified: behind a sign-up. The paid Growth plan is bought by credit card only

reliability_note: the allowance is a lifetime total: once it is used up the plan has to be upgraded, and the API answers HTTP 456 when a character quota is used up
confidence_note: the 1,000,000 character one-time limit and its non-reset are quoted from the vendor's help centre and pricing page; the sign-up form fields are read from the sign-up page; step 2 of the sign-up and the host of a Developer key are behind a sign-up and unverified.

evidence.proved: the Developer plan is free with a total translation limit of 1,000,000 characters
evidence.quote: The DeepL API Developer plan allows developers to try out DeepL’s API for free, with a total translation limit of 1,000,000 characters.

evidence.proved: the Developer allowance does not reset, so it is a one-time credit
evidence.quote: Once this limit has been reached, **it will not reset **and you will need to upgrade to the DeepL API Growth plan.

evidence.proved: the pricing page lists the Developer plan as a one-time credit of 1 million characters
the plan comparison gives the Developer character usage limit as 1 million
evidence.quote: | Character usage limit | 1 million | 50 million per month | Unlimited 1 |

evidence.proved: API plans are paid for by credit card only, which is what upgrading from Developer to Growth takes
evidence.quote: For API plans, we accept payment by credit card only.

evidence.proved: the Developer sign-up page offers 1 million characters for free
the sign-up form has a password field, next to an email field
evidence.quote: Use at least 8 characters for your password

evidence.proved: the sign-up form asks for an age confirmation and is step 1 of a 3 step flow
evidence.quote: I confirm that I am over the age of 14.

evidence.proved: the total request size limit is 128 KiB
the API language list has 126 entries
HTTP 456 is the answer when a usage limit is reached
evidence.quote: * HTTP 456: quota exceeded. The request would take the account or API key past one of its usage limits.

evidence.proved: the DeepL API host answers an unauthenticated request with HTTP 403 and names the key header, so there is no keyless route
evidence.quote: Missing Authorization header, expected 'Authorization: DeepL-Auth-Key <API key>'.

binding_note: the 1,000,000 character lifetime total is the limit that decides; it does not reset
notes: Supported languages: the API language page lists 126 entries (for example Acehnese, Afrikaans, Albanian, Arabic through Zulu), retrievable from the /v3/languages endpoint; features such as glossaries cover only some of them. Character limit per request: 128 KiB total request size; the API counts source characters, and document formats bill a minimum of 50,000 characters per document. Not keyless: every request needs an API key.
